- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% below recent 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model tends to overestimate — apply downward bias of 3–7% to forecast mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — add 2–5% to forecast for first 7 days if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3+ after -0.5), model lags — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply 5–10% upward bias to catch momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be 10–15% below recent 14-day low, not 30-day low.
